body.x: As AI servers, electric vehicle electronics, robot actuators and semiconductor equipment become more powerful, they give off more heat. Heat lowers efficiency, shortens the life of components and raises the risk of fire. Paints made with organic binders can be formulated to shed heat, but they can still burn.

GinnoLab Co., Ltd., a materials company with its address at Seoul Startup Hub in Mapo-gu, Seoul, says it started from that fire problem. Led by CEO Jinho Yoon, the company will take part in FIX 2026 through the PNP Korea Expo to show how its coatings can be applied to equipment and components in future mobility, robotics, semiconductors and electronics.

According to GinnoLab, Yoon, who has eight years of experience in nanomaterials, began developing a coating that does not burn after fires damaged his family's property and factory. The company says that work on flame-retardant, heat-resistant inorganic binders grew into today's heat-dissipation and thermal-insulation coatings. GinnoLab was founded in June 2021 in Wonju, Gangwon Province, and operates its corporate R&D center at Seoul Startup Hub Gongdeok. Yoon leads the company with CTO Cheolheon Park, Head of R&D Giho Kim and COO Gibeom Kwon. Its core technology comes from a technology transfer from the Korea Institute of Machinery & Materials (KIMM), and the company says it holds five patents, including registered patents and pending applications.

The company describes its product as a nano-ceramic inorganic coating reinforced with graphene and boron nitride (BN). It says it disperses ceramic materials such as BN, alumina and silicon carbide (SiC) evenly in a water-based inorganic binder, with graphene as a reinforcing agent, and tailors products for flame retardancy, heat dissipation or thermal insulation from a single binder platform. Because the binder is ceramic and inorganic, the company says, the coating does not burn, whereas ordinary organic paints remain combustible even when a heat-dissipation function is added.

GinnoLab will exhibit three coatings and one product in development. GN-RC900 is a 25 to 50 µm water-based radiative cooling coating that lowers equipment surface temperature and is also non-combustible. GN-I500 is a high-temperature insulation for pipes and equipment in steel and chemical plants. GN-F1000 is a non-combustible coating for building materials and equipment surfaces. GINOTIM, still in development, is a BN-based thermal interface material for AI-server semiconductor packages, being developed through the company's TIPS project. The company also says it is advancing dispersion technology for graphene platelets, hexagonal BN (h-BN) and boron nitride nanotubes (BNNT).

GinnoLab says its coatings fit existing painting lines without new equipment, that it tunes formulations using a database of more than 320 formulation and process conditions, and that volume production runs through an exclusive OEM partner. It reports revenue of about KRW 2.1 billion for 2024 and says it has been profitable for four consecutive years since 2022. In a proof of concept (PoC) for outdoor-unit heat-dissipation materials run by a global home-appliance maker, the company says it ranked first among 64 participating companies: the outdoor unit's measured surface temperature was 86.3°C uncoated, 83.3°C with the existing production coating and 80.0°C with GinnoLab's coating. It also says it has received and fulfilled purchase orders from a Korean secondary-battery materials company, is discussing high-temperature insulation and heat-dissipation uses with a major Korean steelmaker, and is preparing test applications at a large food and materials manufacturer's plant.

GinnoLab's target customers, as it describes them, are facility managers at data centers whose cooling equipment drives up power costs, thermal design engineers at home appliance and air-conditioning companies, energy and equipment managers at steel and chemical plants dealing with heat loss, heat spreader design engineers at electronic component makers, and semiconductor back-end and equipment companies concerned with thermal management in AI-server packages.

At FIX 2026, the company says it wants to meet companies in Korea's future mobility, robotics, semiconductor and electronics industries, find joint PoC partners with heat and fire-safety challenges, and build partnerships with auto parts and machinery manufacturers in the Daegu-Gyeongbuk region. It also plans to meet investors and institutions as it pursues Pre-A funding for a new factory and expanded production, and to offer on-site consultations with coated samples and measured data.

GinnoLab's overseas business is mainly technology licensing and PoC projects. In Japan, it signed a technology license agreement with a Japanese materials company and, in 2026, a nondisclosure agreement (NDA) with a global Japanese electronic components maker, with which it is discussing a PoC applying its coating to heat spreaders in base station communication modules. It has also taken part in G-Camp Tokyo (Plug and Play Shibuya) and SusHi Tech Tokyo, and has run PoCs in Korea, Japan and Germany. The U.S. is not yet an export market. In 2026 the company joined the Portland "Silicon Forest" entry program in Oregon, where it met local semiconductor equipment and device companies. It is setting up a U.S. entity, Ginno LLC, and was selected for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Startup Battlefield 200, held in San Francisco in October 2026.

Its priority export markets are the U.S., Japan and Europe led by Germany. In the U.S., it points to AI data center investment and the need to manage heat in servers and cooling equipment, and aims to start PoCs with local semiconductor equipment and data center companies. In Japan, it sees steady demand for component-level heat dissipation and plans step-by-step verification backed by measured data because, it says, Japanese companies value long-term trust. In Germany and Europe, it cites automotive and industrial equipment manufacturing and strict energy-efficiency and fire-safety rules for buildings and equipment.

The company lists four difficulties. Certification and testing standards differ by country and application, and Korean test reports often cannot be presented abroad as they are. Adopting a coating also depends on process conditions such as the number of coats and drying time, and in one overseas PoC, drying time did not fit the customer's mass-production process, so the target application had to be adjusted. With a team of five, it lacks staff to support overseas customers on site. Finally, new materials go through several stages of verification, so reaching decision-makers at large overseas companies takes time. GinnoLab says it is using export vouchers, the KOSME overseas branch program and overseas market-entry programs to address these challenges.

Its plan has three parts. On production, it intends to build its own base with a new factory and equipment in an industrial complex in Taebaek, Gangwon Province, and is raising a Pre-A round for that purpose. Overseas, it plans to complete Ginno LLC in 2026, pursue PoCs with data center and semiconductor equipment companies through TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, continue with its Japanese license partner and the electronic components PoC, and prepare the certification tests each market requires. On products, it will extend GN-RC900, GN-I500 and GN-F1000 from data centers and home appliances to vehicle electronics, robotics, semiconductor equipment, steel and chemical plants and buildings. Over the long term, it aims to convert PoCs into supply contracts, raise the share of overseas revenue and target a KOSDAQ listing in 2030.

GinnoLab says it closed a seed investment in 2026 from the Kangwon National University-Trigger Gangwon Future Growth Venture Fund and was selected for TIPS with KNU Technology Holdings as its operating partner. It is carrying out a Ministry of SMEs and Startups global R&D project, graduated from the 13th cohort of the Youth Startup Academy and won the grand prize at the 7th NextUnicorn Project.

Now in its third year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Technology Expo) is a future-industry exhibition that brings together and connects innovative technologies in future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It runs from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," the exhibition shares industry trends and core technologies through AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by experts from Korea and abroad, and networking programs.
